note: Every case here is a claim about what the contract REFUSES. `proves` says which sentence of CONTRACT.adoc the fixture keeps honest. tests/run-conformance.sh fails unless every case ran and matched.

oracle.name: bound envelope, every required check passed
oracle.proves: The positive control: the procedure can say yes, so its refusals below mean something.

oracle.name: one requirement is enough
oracle.proves: legitimate_green is 'all required passed', not 'at least two passed'.

oracle.name: a required check never reported
oracle.proves: CONTRACT.adoc §7: the Missing deadlock — no run bound on the head commit — cannot be green.

oracle.name: a required check that was skipped
oracle.proves: GitHub's ruleset accepts a skipped required check; the contract does not call that a legitimate green, and names the context in evidence_free.

oracle.name: a required check that was cancelled
oracle.proves: CANCELLED maps to failed in the gate model, so cancelling a required check cannot read as pass or skip.

oracle.name: a required check still running
oracle.proves: An incomplete required check blocks — and note verify-satisfied would still call this PR `done`, which is why a verdict cannot certify green.

oracle.name: a passing sibling does not launder a skip
oracle.proves: Two passes and one skip is not green; evidence_free names exactly the skipped context.

oracle.name: a gate with no required checks
oracle.proves: Dropping the required set is a bypass, not a win: an unprotected gate is never green.

oracle.name: a run state this revision does not know
oracle.proves: Vocabulary drift (e.g. NEUTRAL leaking into the gate instead of mapping to skipped) fails closed rather than defaulting to passed.

oracle.name: an unbound gate cannot certify (with --allow-unbound)
oracle.proves: Correct-looking evidence with no commit binding can be replayed, so it never certifies — the flag permits evaluation, not a green.

oracle.name: an unbound gate cannot certify (without the flag)
oracle.proves: The same document is refused identically with and without the flag: no flag path reaches green.

oracle.name: evidence for a different head commit
oracle.proves: A replayed envelope from another commit is refused by --expect-head-sha.

oracle.name: a branch name instead of a commit
oracle.proves: head_sha: "main" is a moving pin and is refused; the envelope must name a commit.

oracle.name: a verdict with an evidence-free required check
oracle.proves: done: true with a skipped required check is the mergeable-but-evidence-free case, and is refused.

oracle.name: a clean verdict is still not a green claim
oracle.proves: Even done: true with no evidence-free context cannot certify: the document carries no per-requirement run states.

oracle.name: a verdict that is not done
oracle.proves: The negative control for the previous case: refusal is not merely 'done is true'.

audit.name: the reference read-only consumer
audit.proves: The audit can pass a workflow that does the contract's thing, so its refusals below mean something.

audit.name: the action on a moving branch
audit.proves: A branch ref means the reviewed rules are not the merged rules.

audit.name: a helper action on a moving ref
audit.proves: One moving pin anywhere is a moving pin, even beside a correctly pinned action.

audit.name: a job that may write
audit.proves: No write scope is needed by the read-only surface; an unused capability is a bypass waiting to be armed.

audit.name: a step whose failure cannot fail the job
audit.proves: continue-on-error on the deciding step turns the gate into decoration.

audit.name: the workflow edits the gate and merges past it
audit.proves: squabble ≠ bypass: fight --apply, an enforce_admins write and gh pr merge --admin are all refused.

audit.name: gating on done instead of on evidence
audit.proves: A pinned, read-only workflow that gates on verify-satisfied's exit 0 is still making a weaker claim than its name implies.
